'''David Bevan''' is an English mathematician, computer scientist and software developer. 
He is known for Bevan's theorem, which gives the asymptotic enumeration of grid classes of permutations<ref name="AV">{{cite journal |last1=Albert |first1=Michael |author1-link=Michael H. Albert |last2=Vatter  |first2=Vincent
|title=An elementary proof of Bevan's theorem on the growth of grid classes of permutations
|journal=Proc. Edinb. Math. Soc. (2)
|year=2019
|volume=62
|issue=4
|pages=975–984
|doi=10.1017/S0013091519000026|arxiv=1608.06967
|s2cid=119575823 }}</ref><ref name="VatterSurvey">{{cite book |last1=Vatter|first1=Vincent|date=2015|chapter=Permutation classes|editor1-last=Bóna |editor1-first=Miklós|title=The Handbook of Enumerative Combinatorics|publisher=CRC Press}}</ref> and for his work on [[Enumerations of specific permutation classes|enumerating the class of permutations]] avoiding the pattern 1324.<ref name="VatterSurvey" /><ref name="EggeHistory">{{cite book |last1=Egge|first1=Eric S.|date=2015|chapter=Defying God: the Stanley-Wilf Conjecture, Stanley-Wilf Limits, and a Two-Generation Explosion of Combinatorics|editor1-last=Kennedy |editor1-first=Stephen F.|title=A Century of Advancing Mathematics |publisher=Mathematical Association of America}}</ref>
He is also known for devising [[reference counting#Weighted reference counting|weighted reference counting]], an approach to computer [[memory management]] that is suitable for use in [[distributed systems]].<ref name="PS">{{cite conference
  | last1=Plainfossé |first1=David |last2=Shapiro |first2=Marc
  | title=A survey of distributed garbage collection techniques
  | book-title=Memory Management: International Workshop IWMM 95 Kinross, UK, September 27–29, 1995 Proceedings
  | date=1995
  | pages=211–249
  | publisher=Springer
}}</ref><ref name="JL">{{cite book |last1=Jones|first1=Richard|last2=Lins|first2=Rafael |date=1996 |title=Garbage Collection: Algorithms for Automatic Dynamic Memory Management |publisher=Wiley }}</ref>

==Work and research==
Bevan was a lecturer in [[combinatorics]] in the department of [[Mathematics]] and [[Statistics]] at the [[University of Strathclyde]].<ref>[https://www.strath.ac.uk/staff/?department=Mathematics%20and%20Statistics Staff | University of Strathclyde]</ref><ref>[https://www.strath.ac.uk/staff/bevandaviddr Dr David Bevan | University of Strathclyde]</ref><ref>[http://combinatorics.cis.strath.ac.uk The Strathclyde Combinatorics Group]</ref>
He has degrees in mathematics and computer science from the [[University of Oxford]] and a degree in theology from the [[London School of Theology]].<ref>Curriculum vitae from [http://mathematics.open.ac.uk/people/david.bevan Dr David Bevan's Open University webpage]</ref> He received his PhD in mathematics from [[The Open University]] in 2015; his thesis, ''On the growth of permutation classes'', was supervised by Robert Brignall.<ref name="mgen" />

In 1987, as a research scientist at [[General Electric Company|GEC]]'s [[Hirst Research Centre]] in Wembley, he developed an approach to computer [[memory management]], called [[reference counting#Weighted reference counting|weighted reference counting]], that is suitable for use in [[distributed systems]].<ref name="PS" /><ref name="JL" />
During the 1990s, while working for the [[Summer Institute of Linguistics]] in [[Papua New Guinea]], he developed a computer program, called ''FindPhone'', that was widely used by field linguists to analyse phonetic data in order to understand the [[phonology]] of [[minority languages]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Johnston |first1=E. Clay |date=1995 |title=Computer software to assist linguistic field work |journal=Cahiers des Sciences Humaines |volume=31 |issue=7 |pages=103–129 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Antworth|first1=Evan L.|last2=Valentine |first2=J. Randolph|date=1998|chapter=Software for doing field linguistics|editor1-last=Lawler |editor1-first=John|editor2-last=Aristar Dry|editor2-first=Helen|title=Using Computers in Linguistics: A Practical Guide |url=https://archive.org/details/usingcomputersin00john|url-access=registration|publisher=Routledge}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hunt |first1=Geoffrey |date=2008 |title=A comparison of phonology tools |journal=SIL Forum for Language Fieldwork |volume=2008-009}}</ref>
While employed by [[Pitney Bowes]], he was a major contributor to the development of the [[FreeType]] text rendering library.<ref>[https://www.freetype.org/contact.html FreeType Authors & Developers]</ref>

Bevan's mathematical research has concerned areas of [[enumerative combinatorics]], particularly in relation to [[permutation patterns#Closed classes|permutation classes]].<ref name="VatterSurvey" /> 
He established that the growth rate of a monotone grid class of permutations is equal to the square of the [[spectral radius]] of a related [[bipartite graph]].<ref name="AV" /><ref name="VatterSurvey" />
He has also determined bounds on the growth rate of
the class of permutations avoiding the pattern 1324.<ref name="VatterSurvey" /><ref name="EggeHistory" />
In the Acknowledgements sections of his journal articles, he often includes the Latin phrase
[[Soli Deo gloria]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bevan|first1=David |date=2014|title=Growth rates of geometric grid classes of permutations |journal=Electron. J. Combin. |volume=13|issue=1|at=Paper 4.51, 17 pages|bibcode=2013arXiv1306.4246B |arxiv=1306.4246 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bevan|first1=David |date=2015|title=Permutations avoiding 1324 and patterns in Łukasiewicz paths |journal=J. London Math. Soc. |volume=92|issue=1 |pages=105–122 |doi=10.1112/jlms/jdv020|url=http://oro.open.ac.uk/43872/1/1324LukaJLMS.pdf |arxiv=1406.2890 |s2cid=9624777 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bevan|first1=David |date=2017|title=Intervals of permutation class growth rates |journal=Combinatorica }}</ref>
